newsitem.title: USA: Oregon to save $50 mln with S&P upgrade -Treasurer.
newsitem.headline: Oregon to save $50 mln with S&P upgrade -Treasurer.

text.p: Oregon Treasurer Jim Hill said on Tuesday an upgrade of state debt by Standard & Poor's Corp would save taxpayers about $50 million annually in interest on state bonds.

"It means real savings for the people of Oregon," Hill said. "This upgrade will save taxpayers money by reducing the cost of finance-needed projects, including schools, prisons, road construction, veteran home loans, elderly and disabled housing projects and higher education facilities."
S&P said Monday it raised its rating to AA from AA-minus on Oregon's $3.7 billion of general obligation bonds.
The rating agency also adjusted the state's outlook to stable.
The upgrade reflected the state's improved revenue performance and the likelihood that the state would exceed budget targets for the 1995-1997 biennium, S&P said.
Hill told a press conference that the upgrade would also lower the cost of prison expansion because certificates of participation were also upgraded.
"This bond rating improvement has been a long time in coming," Hill said.
